sources.title: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC, tachyarrhythmia sections and Table 2 (AHA; Wigginton JG, et al. Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithm (AHA 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC)
Electrical Cardioversion Algorithm (AHA 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC)

q_sinus.text: Tachycardia with a pulse. Is it likely sinus tachycardia (P before every QRS, gradual onset, obvious driver)?

q_stable.text: Is the arrhythmia (usually HR 150 or more) causing low BP, altered mentation, shock, ischaemic chest pain or acute heart failure?

q_unstable_type.text: Unstable. Is it polymorphic VT (irregular, wide, changing QRS shape)?

answers.label: Irregular (e.g. AF, flutter with variable block)
Reduced EF or decompensated heart failure
AF with known bundle branch block

e_sinus.title: Sinus tachycardia
actions: Treat the driver: hypovolaemia, bleeding, sepsis, fever, pain, hypoxia, anaemia, PE, drug withdrawal.
Do not cardiovert.
Reassess the heart rate as the cause is treated.
cautions: This node is standard practice, not from the cited guideline (the AHA algorithm assumes a non-sinus tachyarrhythmia).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_sync.title: Unstable: synchronised cardioversion
actions: Synchronised cardioversion now; sedate whenever feasible.
Starting energy (AHA 2025 cardioversion algorithm): AF 200 J; atrial flutter 200 J; narrow-complex tachycardia 100 J; monomorphic VT 100 J.
If device energy guidance is unknown, use the maximum setting.
Regular narrow QRS: adenosine may be tried while preparing to cardiovert.
If it fails: raise the energy, add an antiarrhythmic, look for a cause, get expert help.
cautions: Re-select sync mode before each shock; if sync fails and the patient is critical, switch to unsynchronised shocks.
Have suction, airway equipment, IV access and SpO2 monitoring at the bedside.
Energies are device-dependent: check your defibrillator's guidance.
If pre-excitation is possible (irregular wide QRS, pre-excited AF): no AV-nodal blockers and no IV amiodarone (harm, AHA 2025). If cardioversion fails, repeat at higher energy and get expert help.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_poly.title: Polymorphic VT / torsades
actions: Unstable or pulseless: immediate unsynchronised shock (defibrillation) at the maximum setting.
If pulseless: go to the pathway: Adult cardiac arrest and post-ROSC care.
Recurrent torsades with long QT: magnesium may be considered.
Stop QT-prolonging drugs; correct potassium and magnesium; treat bradycardia that triggers it.
cautions: Magnesium dose is not given in the AHA text reviewed: use the local protocol.
Routine magnesium in polymorphic VT with a normal QT gives no benefit.
Urgent cardiology input.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_svt.title: Stable regular narrow-QRS tachycardia
actions: Vagal manoeuvre first; modified Valsalva techniques terminate more episodes than standard Valsalva (AHA 2025).
Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push with saline flush; if needed, 12 mg.
If not terminated or it recurs: beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker.
Record the ECG during adenosine; get expert input.
cautions: A lower adenosine dose (1 mg) may be enough via a central line or after heart transplant.
Carotid massage: avoid with carotid disease (stroke risk).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_af_hf.title: AF/flutter with reduced EF or decompensated HF
actions: Amiodarone is reasonable for rate control in critically ill patients: 300 mg IV over 1 hour, then 10-50 mg/h over 24 hours (fixed doses, not weight-based).
Digoxin as an adjunct: 0.25 mg IV, repeated to a maximum of 1.5 mg in 24 hours.
Treat triggers: sepsis, hypovolaemia, electrolytes, ischaemia.
If it becomes unstable: synchronised cardioversion.
cautions: Do not give diltiazem/verapamil or IV beta-blockers in decompensated HF with reduced LV function (harm).
Digoxin: caution in renal impairment.
Amiodarone may convert the rhythm: consider thromboembolic risk and anticoagulation per local protocol (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_af_rate.title: Stable AF/flutter: rate control
actions: Beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker (AHA 2025 Table 2 doses):
Metoprolol 2.5-5 mg IV over 2 min, up to 3 doses.
Esmolol 500 mcg/kg IV over 1 min, then 50-300 mcg/kg/min (both weight-based).
Diltiazem bolus 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 min (weight-based).
Then diltiazem infusion 5-10 mg/h (not weight-based).
Verapamil 0.075-0.15 mg/kg IV over 2 min; may repeat once after 30 min.
Treat triggers: sepsis, hypovolaemia, pain, electrolytes.
cautions: Avoid calcium channel blockers in hypotension, heart failure, cardiomyopathy or ACS.
Never use AV-nodal blockers if pre-excitation is suspected.
Before any cardioversion: consider thromboembolic risk and anticoagulation per local protocol (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Check which agents are on the local formulary (e.g. diltiazem IV availability).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_wct.title: Stable regular monomorphic wide-QRS tachycardia
actions: Get expert help early.
Adenosine may be considered only if regular and monomorphic.
Antiarrhythmic infusion: amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 min, repeat if VT recurs, then 1 mg/min for the first 6 hours (fixed doses, not weight-based).

Or procainamide loading infusion 20-50 mg/min (not weight-based) until the arrhythmia stops, hypotension occurs, QRS widens by more than 50%, or a total of 17 mg/kg (weight-based maximum) has been given.
Then procainamide maintenance infusion 1-4 mg/min (not weight-based).
If it becomes unstable: synchronised cardioversion (100 J starting energy).
cautions: Do not give verapamil or diltiazem in wide-QRS tachycardia (harm).
Avoid procainamide with long QT or heart failure.
Procainamide availability locally: check formulary.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_preexc.title: Pre-excited AF (suspected WPW)
actions: Cardioversion is recommended (synchronised; AF starting energy 200 J).
Urgent cardiology / electrophysiology input.
cautions: Do not give digoxin, diltiazem/verapamil, beta-blockers or IV amiodarone (harm, AHA 2025). Adenosine is also harmful in irregular wide-QRS tachycardia.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_af_hypo.title: AF/flutter with hypotension or on vasopressors
actions: If the arrhythmia is causing the hypotension: treat as unstable and cardiovert (go back and choose 'unstable').
Otherwise, amiodarone is reasonable for rate control in critically ill patients: 300 mg IV over 1 hour, then 10-50 mg/h over 24 hours (fixed doses, not weight-based; AHA 2025 Table 2).
Digoxin as an adjunct: 0.25 mg IV, repeated to a maximum of 1.5 mg in 24 hours.
Treat triggers: sepsis, hypovolaemia, electrolytes, ischaemia.
cautions: Avoid diltiazem and verapamil in hypotension (AHA 2025 Table 2).
No AHA hypotension-specific caution for beta-blockers was found: senior decision.
No AV-nodal blockers or IV amiodarone if pre-excitation is suspected.
Digoxin: caution in renal impairment.
Before any cardioversion: consider thromboembolic risk and anticoagulation per local protocol (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.
